method: From Kalshi legs priced 30–85¢ with edge ≥ about −2.5 and no flags (one per game), a leg was kept only when at least two of these agreed and none disagreed: Polymarket's top sports traders on its side, a published expert pick or model (read today or in yesterday's run), and concrete news/matchup reasoning. The dump's expert matching came back empty again, so experts were matched by hand against picks/latest.json and yesterday's archive. Dropped as conflicts: Steelers/Bengals (about $15k of top-trader money on Cincinnati −3.5, but outlets split three to two), Bills/Jets (outlets split), Kraken/Hurricanes (two outlets and $40k on Carolina, one outlet on Seattle), Wake Forest +10.5 (four outlets for, NBC Sports on SMU), Colts and Chiefs (outlets on them but both moneylines flagged for moving 5+ points against since open), and Nets/Grizzlies (outlets on Memphis −5.5 but Kalshi now prices it near a pick'em, so their numbers look stale). Saturday is covered by college football, UFC 334 and NHL; Sunday by two NFL legs. Sunday NBA and NHL had no free published picks yet.
honest: Every leg costs slightly more than fair, so expected return is slightly negative and gets worse with every leg you add.

ladder.label: Under 39.5
ladder.why: Three outlets take the under 38.5: Action Network's Greg Liodice (Michigan has gone under this number in 5 of 9), FanDuel Research (two strong defenses against weak offenses) and VSiN's Steve Makinen (both offenses struggling, Michigan turnover problems). Top traders hold about $5.7k on the under vs $1.8k on the over.

sources.name: Action Network via Yahoo / Greg Liodice (under 38.5)

ladder.label: South Carolina Gamecocks −7.5
ladder.why: VSiN's Steve Makinen and Athlon's Steven Lassan both take South Carolina −7.5: the Gamecocks are on a four-game ATS run and Arkansas has one SEC win. Top traders hold about $6.5k on this side vs $347 against. Risk: Athlon flags LaNorris Sellers (ankle) as questionable.

sources.name: Athlon via Yahoo / Steven Lassan (South Carolina −7.5)

ladder.label: Carolina Panthers
ladder.why: Yahoo's Matt De Lima takes Carolina +2.5, rating the Panthers slightly better on both sides of the ball (projects 27-24). Top traders hold about $3.3k on the Panthers moneyline with nothing against. Priced near a coin flip.

sources.name: Yahoo Sports (The Big Lead) / Matt De Lima (Panthers +2.5)

ladder.label: Auburn Tigers −3.5
ladder.why: Action Network's Doug Ziefel takes Auburn (−2.5 when published), citing Auburn's late-game resilience and Byrum Brown against a Mississippi State team on a five-game skid with injuries. Top traders hold about $3.5k on Auburn −3.5 with nothing against; the extra point vs his number is the risk.

sources.name: Action Network via Yahoo / Doug Ziefel (Auburn −2.5)

ladder.label: Kentucky Wildcats −2.5
ladder.why: DraftKings Network's Julian Edlow takes Kentucky −3: Florida is 1-4 since a 4-0 start and scored 15 points in its last two games, and Kentucky has been strong at home. Top traders hold about $1.2k on this line (and about $7.2k on the Kentucky moneyline).

ladder.label: Uroš Medić
ladder.why: Covers' Joe Osborne picks Medić: four straight first-round knockouts (all inside 79 seconds), better striking numbers, and Holland 3-4 in his last seven. Top traders hold about $5k on Medić vs $834 on Holland. Counterpoint: Holland has a 10-inch reach edge and has never been knocked out in the UFC.

ladder.why: Action Network's Tanner McGrath takes Kansas State +10.5 on a 'road dog with wind' system: strong wind should limit passing and help a big road underdog stay close. Top traders hold about $1.2k on this side with nothing against.

sources.name: Action Network via Yahoo / Tanner McGrath (Kansas State +10.5)

ladder.label: New Mexico Lobos −14.5
ladder.why: Covers' Rob Paul takes New Mexico −14.5, arguing UNLV doesn't have the quarterback play to keep it close. Top traders hold about $1.4k on New Mexico vs $361 against.

ladder.label: Calgary Flames
ladder.why: Dimers' model gives Calgary a 41.2% win chance vs about 37.5% implied, its best value bet in this game. Top traders hold about $14.8k on the Flames with nothing on LA. A longshot, so it sits late in the ladder.

ladder.label: Jacksonville Jaguars
ladder.why: Sports Illustrated's Iain MacMillan (Jaguars −9.5) and Yahoo's Matt De Lima (Jaguars −10.5, projects 30-13) both expect a lopsided win: Jacksonville tops DVOA and Tennessee is badly outmatched. Top traders hold about $10.6k on the Jaguars vs $2.1k against. A short favourite, so it sits last.

sources.name: Yahoo Sports (The Big Lead) / Matt De Lima (Jaguars −10.5)
